guard.negative_proof: tests/architecture/redirects-platform-limits.test.mjs run against public/_redirects at 34beed0 fails with "dynamic rules 108 > 100", the same count as the Cloudflare error (line 131 is the 101st rule from the first :slug rule); a synthetic file with one dynamic rule above 101 static rules also fails.

reuse_boundary: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets _redirects (2,000 static, 100 dynamic, 2,100 total). Any provider rule that wrangler deploy --dry-run does not evaluate needs its own source guard; the dry-run passing is not evidence for it.
root_cause: Cloudflare counts every _redirects rule from the first dynamic rule (placeholder or splat) onward as dynamic. Two /products/:slug rules sat near the top of the file, so once #681 added four static rules the dynamic count reached 108 and the server-side upload check rejected the deploy. Local gates and wrangler deploy --dry-run do not run that check, and the failure was only visible in the Workers Builds log, which agents could not read, so it took a day to find.
rule: Dynamic _redirects rules go last, and the platform limits are counted in source the way Cloudflare counts them. A failed Workers Build is diagnosed from its build log before guessing at provider-side causes.
title: Cloudflare _redirects dynamic-rule limit broke every deploy from #681
trigger: 2026-10-25: every Cloudflare Workers Build on main from 8a22dfb (#681) to 34beed0 failed at wrangler deploy with "Maximum number of dynamic _redirects rules limit of 100 exceeded [code: 100324]", so production kept serving the #674 build (for example /en/products/vungtaylai/ returned 404).
